reasons.text: Buys feedstock inside a closed loop of 3 recyclers trading the same material (25% of its feedstock)
Category III share of certificates is 41%, +39% versus what its process route can produce
100% of certificate tonnes were sold below the cost of recycling (average 0.47x the cost floor)
45% of feedstock comes from collectors invoicing far beyond their declared capacity
Certificates claim more than the declared monthly capacity in 19% of months
21% of purchase invoices have suspiciously round tonnages (typical plant: about 2%)

inspection_checklist: Trace the material flow between the plants in the loop (weighbridge slips, vehicle GPS); the same tonnes may be invoiced round a ring.
Cross-check the certificate generation dates and category mix against the plant's process route and stock registers.
Ask for the plant's cost sheet; certificates priced below the cost of recycling imply the processing cost was never incurred.
Visit the named collectors: confirm premises, vehicles and storage; check their registration dates and sales to other buyers.
Check installed machinery and shift records against the declared capacity; request production registers for the flagged months.
Physically verify a sample of purchase invoices with the sellers (weighbridge slips, e-way bills, vehicle logs).
